title: Financial Snapshot: Cash, Debt, and Audit Status
subtitle: Summary of year-end liquidity, leverage, and audit qualification

overview.text: The entity reported a year-end cash position of USD 4 million (F1) and a total debt level of USD 9 million (F2). These figures indicate the company’s immediate liquidity and leverage position at the reporting date.

The audit opinion was qualified because inventory could not be verified (F3, F4). A qualified opinion means the auditor could not obtain sufficient evidence for a specific area, in this case inventory, which limits the assurance provided by the audit.

highlights.text: Year-end cash stood at USD 4 million (F1).
Total debt was reported at USD 9 million (F2).
The audit opinion was qualified due to unverified inventory (F3, F4).

risks.text: Inventory could not be verified, leading to a qualified audit opinion (F3, F4). This uncertainty affects the reliability of financial statements related to inventory valuation.
Total debt of USD 9 million exceeds year-end cash of USD 4 million (F1, F2), indicating a net debt position that may pressure liquidity.

questions: What specific controls failed to allow inventory verification, and what remediation is planned?
How does the USD 9 million debt level impact the company's ability to service obligations given the USD 4 million cash position?
What is the expected timeline for resolving the inventory verification issue to remove the audit qualification?
